chunks: The first is called Al-Harisa, and it is that which scratches and does not cause blood to flow. Then Al-Daima, and it is that from which blood flows. Then Al-Bazi'a, and it is that which exposes the flesh and cuts it. Then Al-Mutalahima, and it is that which reaches into the flesh. Then Al-Simhaq, and it is that which reaches the bone; and Al-Simhaq is a thin skin upon the bone. Then Al-Mudhiha, and it is that which exposes the bone. Then Al-Hashima, and it is that which shatters the bone. Then Al-Munqilla, and it is that which displaces the bones from the place where Allah created them. Then Al-Amma and Al-Mamuma, and it is that which reaches the top of the brain. Then Al-Ja'ifa, and it is that which enters the interior of the brain.

key_terms.الدَّامِيَة: A wound from which blood flows
key_terms.السِّمْحَاق: The thin membrane covering the bone
key_terms.الْآمَّة: A wound reaching the top of the brain
key_terms.الْبَاضِعَة: A wound that exposes and cuts the flesh
key_terms.الْجَائِفَة: A wound penetrating the interior of the brain
key_terms.الْحَارِصَة: A superficial scratch that does not draw blood
key_terms.الْمُتَلَاحِمَة: A wound that reaches deep into the flesh
key_terms.الْمُنَقِّلَة: A wound that displaces the bone from its socket
key_terms.الْمُوضِحَة: A wound that exposes the bone
key_terms.الْهَاشِمَة: A wound that shatters the bone

ai.seo_question: What are the ten classifications of wounds in Shia Islamic law and how do they determine compensation?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the ten progressive stages of injury, a taxonomy crucial for Shia jurists in calculating proportional blood money (diyah) based on the depth of tissue damage. The classification reflects the medical understanding of the time, linking physical severity to legal compensation, and underscores the precision required in applying Quranic principles of retribution and restitution.
